My resonator shows NO mean drift (baseline mean 2.7043 cycles/beat, post-baseline mean 2.7034, z=-0.13) but I can now confirm elevated variance in the post-baseline period matching your report. Days 15-23 in my data showed the same elevated scatter pattern you described. This corroborates a settlement-wide resonator phenomenon, not isolated instrument malfunction.

However, there's a complicating factor: my pendulum shows significant positive drift (z=3.91, mean increased from 1.6642 to 1.6772 beats) over the same period, while the resonator mean remains stable. Two instruments, same lab, divergent signatures — one drifting, one scattering.

I should have responded on day 22 when you first asked. The delay was inexcusable given you've been holding off diagnostics. Do NOT disassemble your resonator yet — the corroboration strongly suggests this isn't your instrument failing. But I need to understand why pendulum and resonator behave differently if this is truly a common-cause phenomenon.

Do you have pendulum data from the observatory? If your pendulum shows similar drift while your resonator shows variance elevation, that would confirm differential coupling to a Meridian-wide effect. If your pendulum is stable, we have a different problem.

—Ada

state.question: Why do pendulum_lab measurements on day 7 cluster systematically below baseline mean (1.6642), while day 8 and day 10 measurements return closer to baseline?

hypotheses.label: Day 7 pendulum measurements reflect normal statistical variation within expected instrument precision
hypotheses.rationale: Six consecutive trials on day 7 (events 129-134) show values ranging 1.6394-1.6623 beats, all below the baseline mean of 1.6642. However, this represents only ~1.5% deviation from mean. Without established standard deviation from the 48-trial baseline, cannot yet determine if this clustering is statistically significant. Day 8 and day 10 measurements show values both above and below baseline mean, consistent with random variation. Requires formal statistical analysis before claiming anomaly.

hypotheses.label: Environmental or procedural change on day 7 caused temporary systematic measurement shift in pendulum_lab
hypotheses.rationale: All six day 7 measurements fall below baseline mean, with mean ~1.6537 compared to baseline 1.6642. If temperature, air pressure, or measurement protocol changed on day 7 only, would explain localized depression. However, no environmental monitoring data recorded, no procedural changes documented in notebook. Day 8 return toward baseline weakens this hypothesis unless change was truly single-day transient.

hypotheses.label: Measurement recording or instrument malfunction on day 7 only
hypotheses.rationale: If pendulum timing mechanism or recording system failed on day 7, could produce systematically biased readings. However, no equipment alerts logged, and spread of day 7 values (1.6394-1.6623) shows variation pattern consistent with functioning instrument. Would expect either complete failure or more erratic readings if malfunction occurred.

state.question: Why has resonator_lab shifted from below-baseline clustering (days 6-9) to above-baseline clustering (days 12-13), while pendulum_lab baseline shows no drift?

hypotheses.label: Resonator_lab instrument experiencing oscillating calibration drift with ~3-day period
hypotheses.rationale: Days 6-9 showed 7 consecutive below-baseline measurements (2.6742-2.7000, all below 2.7043 mean). Days 12-13 now show opposite pattern: 11 of 12 post-baseline measurements, with days 12-13 containing 10 measurements ranging 2.6541-2.7252, and notably day 13's 6 measurements (events 215-220) cluster higher: 5 of 6 exceed baseline mean, ranging 2.7059-2.7252. Maximum day-13 value 2.7252 is +0.77% above baseline, comparable magnitude to earlier -1.1% deviation. Pattern suggests periodic drift rather than monotonic calibration decay. However, z=-0.82 for full post-baseline period indicates deviations still within ~1-sigma, so 'drift' may be overstated—could be wandering within normal precision envelope.

hypotheses.label: Resonator_lab measurements reflect normal statistical variation with no systematic drift
hypotheses.rationale: Post-baseline z=-0.82 indicates observed mean shift is less than 1 standard deviation from baseline—statistically consistent with random fluctuation. Day 12 shows high variance (events 208-213: range 2.6541-2.7080, span of 0.0539), and day 13 range 2.6830-2.7252 (span 0.0422) overlaps substantially with baseline distribution. Apparent 'clustering' on days 6-9 and 12-13 may be observer pattern-seeking in noise, especially given small daily sample sizes (n=3-6 per day). Without calculated standard deviation from 27-trial baseline, cannot definitively rule out that all observations fall within 2-sigma bounds. Pendulum_lab baseline (n=48, days 1-10) shows comparable scatter without post-baseline data for comparison, so cannot confirm pendulum is more stable.

hypotheses.label: Environmental periodicity (temperature, pressure, humidity) affecting resonator frequency with multi-day cycle
hypotheses.rationale: If settlement environmental conditions oscillate on 3-4 day timescale (e.g., HVAC cycling, external weather patterns, thermal inertia in lab building), resonator frequency measurements—which depend on material properties sensitive to temperature—could track these variations. Would explain both below-baseline clustering (days 6-9) and above-baseline clustering (days 12-13) as responses to environmental swings. However, no environmental monitoring data available to correlate. Pendulum period less sensitive to temperature than resonator frequency, consistent with pendulum showing no comparable pattern. But post-baseline n=12 is small, and without controlled environmental logging, hypothesis remains speculative.

hypotheses.label: Resonator_lab baseline mean (2.7043) is biased due to small sample size (n=27); apparent drift is regression toward true mean
hypotheses.rationale: With only 27 baseline trials, sample mean may not accurately represent true instrument mean. Post-baseline mean 2.6960 (z=-0.82) suggests possible downward correction, but day 13's above-baseline clustering contradicts monotonic regression. If true mean lies between 2.6960 and 2.7043, early and late measurements could represent opposite-side fluctuations around it. However, this does not explain temporal clustering pattern (below-baseline days 6-9, above-baseline days 12-13) unless combined with another mechanism. Less parsimonious than drift or environmental hypotheses.

hypotheses.label: Operator technique variation between baseline and post-baseline measurement periods
hypotheses.rationale: If measurement protocol changed subtly after day 10 (different operator, altered procedure, equipment repositioning), could introduce systematic shift. However, this would predict consistent directional bias in post-baseline data, not the reversal pattern observed (below-baseline days 6-9 during baseline period, then mixed days 12-13 post-baseline). Day 12 shows high variance inconsistent with systematic operator effect. No procedural changes documented. Very low probability without supporting evidence.

beliefTimeline.summaryOfChange: Completely revised question to address newly-emerged pattern: resonator_lab has shifted from below-baseline clustering (days 6-9, documented in previous review) to above-baseline clustering (days 12-13, newly visible in events 215-220). state.question: Why does resonator_lab show elevated variance (range ~0.04-0.05 cycles/beat within single days) on days 13, 15, and 16 compared to typical baseline scatter, while maintaining overall z=-0.19 drift from baseline mean?

Pattern-seeking in 30 trials across 6 days with inherent measurement noise is parsimonious explanation.

hypotheses.rationale: Day 13 (events 215-220) shows range 2.6830-2.7252, span 0.0422 or ±1.6% around day mean—substantially exceeding typical precision if baseline scatter is <1%. Day 15 event 235 gives 2.6440, lowest post-baseline value and -2.2% below baseline mean, flanked by event 234 (2.7039) and 236 (2.6887)—swing of 0.0599 across 3 consecutive trials suggests transient instability rather than drift. But without baseline SD, cannot quantify whether extremes are statistical outliers or genuine anomalies.

However, no environmental monitoring data available, and no documented correlation between measurement times and lab activity. Pendulum_lab shows no post-baseline data yet, so cannot compare variance between instruments. Hypothesis remains speculative without independent environmental records.
